summary: Add a tenant-scoped AI provider account capability (settings CRUD, bounded analytics completion) plus the openai-compatible connector as its first registered ai-family provider, keeping Core and the settings API free of any provider-name branching.

impacts.evidence: ai_provider_accounts is a new tenant-scoped table (organization_id/workspace_id, RLS forced) storing only label/model/base_url/folder_id/enabled/version plus a secrets.Reference; credential bytes never live in Postgres.

The only tenant text sent off-platform is the caller-assembled analytics prompt at analyze-call time; the audit trail intentionally records only account id/provider/outcome, never the prompt or the model's response.
Four additive OpenAPI 0.16.0 operations under /settings/ai-providers(:disable|:analyze); no existing operation changed.
No EventBus schema is published or consumed by this capability.

Frozen Connector/Runtime roots are unchanged. Adds an additive ai family, ai.completion.generate capability, and the openai-compatible provider; dispatch by provider id is confined to internal/platform/builtinruntime, the sole registered provider composition module.

Migration 000012_ai_advisory.sql adds ai_provider_accounts as a normal post-baseline expand migration; 000013_ai_provider_credential_class.sql additively widens the pre-existing secret_references.class CHECK constraint (the same pattern 000011 used) to admit ai_provider_credential. The immutable 000001-000011 pre-v1 squash is unchanged and re-verified byte-identical.

Provider code has no direct network/database/filesystem/process/Core/App authority; all HTTPS calls are host-mediated through builtinruntime's DNS-pinned, public-IP-only transport. Credential bytes are read only inside a host-owned UseSecret callback and are zeroed after use at the API layer.

Account create/disable/analyze are audited as write_sensitive; analyze is capability-gated separately (ai.analyze, manager/operator/admin) from account management. settings.ai_providers.write (create/disable) is admin only; settings.ai_providers.read (list, never returns credential material) extends to manager/operator/viewer for account selection, matching the existing read-broad/write-admin-only pattern used by connectors.accounts.*.
Every create/disable/analyze call is captured with actor, correlation id and a bounded summary (provider, label, ok) that excludes prompt/response text.
This capability performs no remote-state synchronization; there is nothing to reconcile.
Outbound calls use a host-injected transport to a fixed default host (api.openai.com) or an account-configured OpenAI-wire-compatible hostname; no inbound webhook surface is added.
Remote non-2xx responses and empty/malformed completions normalize to a bounded 502 at the API layer; the connector's manifest rate_limit/retry policy bounds concurrency and backoff.

Disabling or deleting an ai_provider_accounts row (soft-disable; DELETE is revoked at the schema level, matching catalog_product_images) immediately stops further analyze calls for that account; no other component depends on this table.

Package tests cover request/response marshaling and manifest/account mismatch rejection; the canonical Task-064 conformance suite passes all thirteen checks (docs/connectors/openai-compatible/conformance-report.json), including sandbox_isolation verified under a privileged Linux runner.
